test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 29 Jan 2022)
subject: general
question: A and B can do a work in {26(2)/(3)} days. B and C together can complete the same work in 48 days, while A and C together can complete the same work in 30 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to complete 60% of the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work (LCM of 80/3, 48, 30) = 240 units.

Efficiencies: (A+B) = 9, (B+C) = 5, (A+C) = 8.

Combined efficiency 2(A+B+C) = 9 + 5 + 8 = 22 ⇒ A+B+C = 11.

Efficiency of A = (A+B+C) − (B+C) = 11 − 5 = 6.

Required time for 60% work = (240 × 60%) ÷ 6 = 144 ÷ 6 = 24 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 26 2/3 days = 80/3 days

Time taken by (B + C) = 48 days

Time taken by (A + C) = 30 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

Total Work = LCM of time taken by individual pairs

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 (A + B)
 80/3
 240
 240 ÷ (80/3) = 9
 
 

 (B + C)
 48
 240 ÷ 48 = 5
 
 

 (A + C)
 30
 240 ÷ 30 = 8
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of efficiencies = (A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 9 + 5 + 8

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 22

⇒ A + B + C = 11

⇒ Efficiency of A = (A + B + C) − (B + C)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 11 − 5 = 6

⇒ 60% of Total Work = 60% × 240 = 0.6 × 240 = 144 units

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 144 ÷ 6 = 24 days

**∴ The correct answer is 24 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Fractions

LCM of (a/b, c/d, e/f) = LCM(a, c, e) ÷ HCF(b, d, f). This is useful when days are given in fractions.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person, which is proportional to (Efficiency × Time).

Combined Efficiency Rule

When pairs (A+B, B+C, C+A) are given, individual efficiencies are found by A = [(A+B) + (A+C) − (B+C)] ÷ 2.</p
